changelogs.description:
Move dsv41flash-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-dspark-disagg-hicache to nightly-dev-cu13-20261111-314bce7c (Dynamo 1.7.0.dev20261110, SGLang 0.0.0.dev1+g314bce7cf), pinned by digest. The agg key stays on nightly-dev-cu13-20261030-302b78cc: on the 20261111 image the NVIDIA megakernel plugin rejects the bundled FlashInfer low-latency block-scaled GEMM at startup.
Add a DEP32 decode point: 6 DEP2 prefill workers and one DEP32 decode worker on 8 nodes at c3018 (decode CUDA graph batch 18, max-running-requests 576, extra slots 80, 32 redundant EPLB experts, total_requests DP balancing, block-wise rejection for the sampled DSpark verify).
Drop 3 prefill workers at c700 and c1228 (DEP16 decode): the DEP32 c3018 point has both higher interactivity and higher throughput per GPU than each of them. Drop 5 prefill workers at c2884 (DEP16 decode): it lies under the line between DEP32 c3018 and 7P c5540.
Set stream-interval 32 on the agg role and on the disagg prefill role, which used the SGLang default of 1; disagg decode already used 32. Agg TP4 c1, c4 and c16 change otherwise not at all; disagg 7P c5540 and 9P c7480 change otherwise only by the image. The agg key is listed so the whole Dynamo + SGLang curve, agg points included, comes from this sweep.

Add GB200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Dynamo + vLLM AgentX curves on vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-aarch64-01fba62-1111d (vLLM main with the merged vllm#66552; arm64 sha256:9aa51d63c0f9e408a6a38df5aaeac2794da5de766d7398035a380bdf3d41389a) with the Dynamo 1.6.0.dev20261010 vLLM sidecar; the aggregated points and the c3018 and c4096 disaggregated decodes use the fused DSpark Markov draft sampler (dspark_fused_markov).
Aggregated TP4 on one node: concurrency 4 (max-num-seqs 8, max-num-active-seqs 1, prefill-schedule-interval 24, deep_select indexer top-k), 10 (max-num-seqs 16, max-num-active-seqs 2) and 16 (max-num-seqs 64, max-num-active-seqs 3), with THP Engram host tables.
Disaggregated DEP4 prefill / DEP16 or DEP32 decode with push NIXL transfer and 2 to 7 async KV loads started per decode step: 3P1D DEP32 at c3018 (max-num-seqs 18), 3P1D DEP16 at c3018 (max-num-seqs 48, 70 GiB CPU KV per prefill rank), 4P1D DEP16 at c4096 (max-num-seqs 64) and 5P1D DEP16 at c5600 (max-num-seqs 112); the others offload up to 90 GiB of CPU KV per prefill rank.

Aggregated: replace the seven TP16 DCP16 points (concurrency 1, 4, 8, 24, 32, 48 and 56) with TP16 DCP8 points at concurrency 1 (EP1, 2 running requests) and 4 (EP4, 8 running requests, mem-fraction-static 0.82), both verifying 8 DFLASH tokens. agg-variants.yaml now holds only the DCP8 design: HiCache 108 GB per rank, Run:ai streamer loading, dist-timeout 3600 and no KV events from the single worker.
Disaggregated: add a 1P2D TP16 point at concurrency 32 (EP4 DCP16 prefill, two TP16 DCP16 decode workers capped at 32 requests) and PP2 points: 1P2D at concurrency 76 and 150, and 1P1D at concurrency 150 and 200. PP2 prefill runs TP8 x PP2 with DCP8 and EP2 and splits the 93 layers 48/45. Its decode runs TP16 as DCP8 x attention DP2 with EP16 DeepGEMM MegaMoE (MXFP8 dispatch, BF16 combine), shared experts at TP8 and 128 (192 at 1P1D concurrency 150) running requests.
Disaggregated: remove the 1P1D TP16 points at concurrency 32 and 48 and the 1P1D EP16 MegaMoE points at concurrency 76 and 96. The 1P1D TP16 concurrency 16 and 1P1D EP16 concurrency 64 points keep their recipes.
Every point keeps the same image, FP32 KDA recurrent state, FP8 KV, DFLASH block verification and the committed golden acceptance curve. The new points size HiCache at 108 GB per rank, load weights with the Run:ai streamer (the PP2 prefill uses the default loader, which supports pipeline parallelism) and publish no KV events from their single prefill or aggregated worker.

Update the image from rocm/atom-dev:nightly_202610121516 to nightly_202611101510 (ATOM e5b74bc86, ROCm 7.2.4) in the master config, and the AToMesh frontend container_image from sha256:a60811a8467b43e3e50e9e9eb8cec34f68b7bca03f8c6dbd6a0ff813dde49d4c to sha256:160a4ec49379e7f1980a4e783254366b1d5c643b012abca57a21c0bcbbfe83a7, the same image.
Replace plain TP2 at concurrency [1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 16, 32, 64] and plain TP4 at [1, 8, 32] with plain TP2 at [1, 2, 16, 32], DTP2 (DP attention) at 64, DEP2 (DP attention plus expert parallelism) at [128, 256] and plain TP4 at [1, 2, 4, 8, 32]. TP2 c4, c6, c8 and c64 are dropped; TP4 c2 and c4 are new.
Switch the KV cache from BF16 to MXFP8 (kv_cache_dtype fp8) at every point; the index cache stays FP4.
Drop max-num-seqs 128, so every point except concurrency 1 runs ATOM's default admission. Concurrency 1 (TP2 and TP4) runs max-num-seqs 2, decode graphs [1, 2] and ATOM_PREFILL_DECODE_INTERVAL=1000000, the C1 recipe of ATOM's recipes/Kimi-K3.md (ROCm/ATOM#2659). The c256 point also captures graph size 256.
Set ATOM_PREFILL_DECODE_INTERVAL per point: 192 at TP2 c2 and TP4 c2, c4 and c8, 96 at TP2 c16, 40 at TP2 c32, 16 at TP4 c32 (unchanged) and 10 at the DP points (previously unset except 4 at TP2 c64 and 16 at TP4 c32).
The DP points add dp-load-balance least_tokens, ATOM_DP_SESSION_AFFINITY=1, ATOM_DP_LB_REQ_EQUIV=512 and GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5, and AIPerf sends the correlation ID as the X-Dynamo-Session-Id header for session affinity.
Every point adds timeout-keep-alive 900 so the server keeps AIPerf's pooled connections open past uvicorn's 5 s default.
The new ATOM brings DeepSeek-V4.1 DP attention (ROCm/ATOM#2376), the V4.1 MXFP8 KV cache with DSpark on an FP8 cache (ROCm/ATOM#2725), DP-attention prefill balancing and graph replay (ROCm/ATOM#2551, #2696, #2697) and the default HIP Mega-MHC kernel on gfx950 (ROCm/ATOM#2568).
No change to the DSpark draft's weight precision: ATOM loads the checkpoint's mtp.0-2 layers as shipped (FP8 E4M3 attention, shared experts and main_proj with 32x32 UE8M0 scales, MXFP4 routed experts, BF16 router, norms and heads) at both images. The draft shares the target's KV pool, so its KV cache follows the target from BF16 to MXFP8.

Add Qwen3.8-Flash-Next FP8 TPU v7 AgentX on one 2x2x1 host (4 chips): one TP8 vLLM engine with expert parallelism, image us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/ironwood-496417/torchtpu-vllm/torchtpu-vllm-prod:infx-qwen38-flash-agentx-za10e (vllm-torchtpu c6fd3ab717)
5 AgentX concurrencies (1, 4, 8, 16, 32), each with its own per-point profile in benchmarks/single_node/agentic/qwen3.8next_fp8_tpuv7_mtp.sh
MTP k=3 with synthetic acceptance length 2.32 (golden AL at k=3) in --speculative-config; draft kept at checkpoint precision; thinking on (model default chat template)
FP8 weights and KV, prefix caching, 8,192 batched tokens, max model length 262,144; whole-step megakernel decode at every point (rows up to 32 below conc 32, up to 64 at conc 32)
conc 32: main-KV DCP 2 with the Mamba tail fold under DCP, request-sharded decode indexer, max-num-seqs 32; SparseCore all-gather offload off
Add the qwen38-weights-snap snapshot (runners/k8s 26-, 27- and populate-qwen38-weights-job.yaml) and clone it from both tpuv7 launchers for Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8

Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Dynamo + vLLM AgentX configs on VR NVL72, DSpark on the MXFP4 checkpoint: six disaggregated points and one aggregated point. Every serving role streams with an interval of 20 tokens.
Image vllm-cu134-vr1111f-b1: the vr1111f Rubin image with the specialized-decode warm-up running after the CuMem weights pool closes, plus opt-in switches (DSpark post-forward CUDA graphs on a NIXL KV consumer, low-batch specialized-decode GEMM paths, wide wo_b publish, fused Lamport consumer with the router GEMM, DFlash padding programs). Points without switches run vr1111f code paths.
DEP4 prefill with one DEP32 decode worker and MXFP4 decode activations: 3P1D c6600 with 5 draft tokens (24 per rank).
One DEP2 prefill worker with TP4 latency-specialized decode workers, 5 draft tokens, CuMem on decode: 1P3D c310 (8 sequences per worker, all specialized-decode switches) and 1P4D c260 (4 per worker, post-forward CUDA graphs).
Mooncake DRAM KV tier (two 465 GiB stores per node, one per NUMA node) with DEP2 prefill workers and a Dynamo KV router without session affinity: 6P1D DEP32 c11000 (5 draft tokens, 52 per rank), 6P1D DEP16 c11500 and 8P1D DEP16 c15800 (3 draft tokens, 216 and 300 per rank).
Aggregated TP8 latency-specialized decode across two nodes, c1, 5 draft tokens, async scheduling depth 6 and a 24-step prefill cadence.
AgentX client: agentx-harness 1.0.14.
